title: Agreement advances Texas gas-plus-nuclear concept to next phase -- ANS / Nuclear Newswire
key_facts: GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy (GVH) and Blue Energy announced on a Thursday an agreement to advance to the engineering design, licensing and safety analysis phase for a potential 'gas-plus-nuclear' plant in Victoria, Texas.
The plant would use GVH BWRX-300 small modular reactors and GE Vernova 7HA.02 gas turbines, subject to a final investment decision in 2027.
By 2030 Blue Energy expects to give a nearby data center about 1 GW of capacity from a pair of gas turbines.
Five BWRX-300 reactors would come on line in 2032, adding about 1.5 GW of new nuclear capacity.
GVH CEO Jason Cooper said combining gas turbines and small reactors is a way of 'bridging between gas and nuclear timelines for project delivery'.
Blue Energy CEO Jake Jurewicz said 'It's about speed, which the data center community and the utilities need right now'.
quote_evidence: On Thursday, the two companies announced an agreement to advance to the engineering design, licensing, and safety analysis phase for a potential plant in Victoria, Texas, complete with GVH BWRX-300 small modular reactors and GE Vernova 7HA.02 gas turbines.
All of this is subject to a final investment decision coming in 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: A plan to power data centers with gas first and small reactors later, still subject to a 2027 investment decision.
